Estimate the Error Model by Restricted Maximum Likelihood

Source: R/reml.R
reml.Rd

Alternates between fitting the mean parameters at a fixed error model and updating the error parameters from the REML stationarity condition, until the error parameters stop moving. Every data point enters with the leverage of that point, see remlLeverage(). Every L2 term of a composed objective is used, so normL2(d1, ...) + normL2(d2, ...) is handled as one dataset.

Usage

reml(
  objfun,
  pars,
  errpars = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  iterlim = 25L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  rankTol = 1e-08,
  optimizer = trust,
  control = NULL,
  cores = getOption("dMod2.cores", 1L),
  ...
)

Arguments

objfun

Objective function built by normL2(), with an error model.

pars

Named numeric starting vector of mean and error parameters.

errpars

Character, the error-model parameters. Default NULL: the symbols of the error equations that appear in pars.

fixed

Named numeric, held fixed throughout. Default NULL.

iterlim

Maximum number of rounds. Default 25.

tol

Convergence threshold on the largest change of an error parameter between two rounds. Default 1e-6.

rankTol

Passed to remlLeverage(). Default 1e-8.

optimizer

Optimizer for the mean step, called as optimizer(objfun, parinit, fixed = , cores = , ...). Default trust().

control

Named list of arguments for optimizer, merged into list(rinit = 0.1, rmax = 10). Default NULL.

cores

Passed to the prediction and the objective. Default getOption("dMod2.cores", 1).

...

Further arguments for objfun in the mean step, passed through optimizer. value.plain is evaluated without them.

Value

A list with components

argument

The full parameter vector.

value

The REML criterion, value.plain + logdet.

value.plain

The objective at argument.

logdet

Log determinant of \(J^\top W J\), see remlLeverage().

errpars

The error-model parameters.

leverage

The data frame returned by remlLeverage().

dof

Effective degrees of freedom per observable.

rank

Effective number of mean parameters.

iterations

Number of rounds.

converged

Logical.

fit

The last mean fit.

Details

Only first-order sensitivities are used. A term acting on the error parameters from outside the data term, such as a prior, is not part of the REML condition; reml() warns when it finds one.

See also

remlLeverage(), normL2()

Examples

# \donttest{
old <- options(dMod2.outdir = tempdir())
f <- addReaction(eqnlist(), from = "A", to = "", rate = "k*A")
x <- Xs(odemodel(f, modelname = "reml_x", compile = FALSE))
g <- Y(c(y = "A"), f = x, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "reml_g",
       compile = FALSE)
e <- Y(c(y = "sigma_y"), f = g, attachInput = FALSE, condition = "C1",
       modelname = "reml_e", compile = FALSE)
p <- P(eqnvec(A = "exp(logA)", k = "exp(logk)", sigma_y = "sigma_y"),
       condition = "C1", modelname = "reml_p", compile = FALSE)
compile(x, g, e, p, output = "reml_example", cores = 1)
#> using C++ compiler: g++
#>   every source : -O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC
#>   2 of 5 also  : -fopenmp

set.seed(1)
times <- seq(0, 5, by = 0.25)
data <- datalist(C1 = data.frame(
  name = "y", time = times, sigma = NA_real_,
  value = 2 * exp(-0.5 * times) + rnorm(length(times), sd = 0.1)))
obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = e)

fit <- reml(obj, c(logA = 0, logk = 0, sigma_y = 1))
fit$argument
#>        logA        logk     sigma_y 
#>  0.67832557 -0.75124935  0.09166024 
fit$dof
#>  y 
#> 19 
head(remlLeverage(obj, fit$argument))
#>   condition time name      sigma    residual   leverage
#> 1        C1 0.00    y 0.09166024  0.03322076 0.39880136
#> 2        C1 0.25    y 0.09166024 -0.03202037 0.24442887
#> 3        C1 0.50    y 0.09166024  0.08245573 0.15525247
#> 4        C1 0.75    y 0.09166024 -0.15077817 0.10691867
#> 5        C1 1.00    y 0.09166024 -0.01658392 0.08322519
#> 6        C1 1.25    y 0.09166024  0.10417243 0.07360126
options(old)
# }
